stories.title: What Was Eli Lilly Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
stories.summary: An investor who put $10,000 into Eli Lilly (LLY) stock on October 14, 2025 held about $15,500 by October 15, 2026. Placing that same sum in the S&P 500 over the identical period would have yielded about $11,790. By mid-2026, two drugs, Zepbound and Mounjaro, accounted for most of the company's sales. How early did those two drugs show up in what Lilly said and filed.

stories.title: Why You Should Think About Palantir Differently Now

Investors paying that premium need to know exactly what they are buying, and the case Palantir makes has evolved. During the fiscal Q3 2024 earnings call, executives highlighted the fast-growing number of U.S. businesses signing on as customers. By the latest call in fiscal Q2 2026, the focus had shifted. So what does management talk up now.

stories.title: Should You Trim Or Add To Your Joby Aviation Position Now?

Joby is not short of money yet, ending June 2026 with about $2.3 billion in cash and short-term investments. So what does Joby sell today, and what is it spending the cash on.

stories.title: Can Trade Desk Stock Bounce Off Its Old Support Again?
stories.summary: Investors holding Trade Desk (TTD) have seen the stock lose 74.1% of its value over the past year, compared with a 17.9% return for the S&P 500. The immediate question is how much further shares might drop. One certainty is the current level: at $13.13 on October 15, the stock sits above the prices where it turned and rallied three times in 2018. How did the stock fare at this price then, and how has it fared in 2026.
